per_question.question: What is the subject matter of Article 1 of the RoHS Directive?
per_question.reference_answer: Article 1 of the RoHS Directive lays down rules on the restriction of the use of hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) with a view to contributing to the protection of human health and the environment, including the environmentally sound recovery and disposal of waste EEE.
per_question.actual_answer: This Directive lays down rules on the restriction of the use of hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) with a view to contributing to the protection of human health and the environment, including the environmentally sound recovery and disposal of waste EEE.

per_question.question: Under RoHS Article 2(1), to which equipment does the Directive apply?
per_question.reference_answer: Subject to paragraph 2, RoHS Article 2(1) says this Directive shall apply to EEE falling within the categories set out in Annex I.
per_question.actual_answer: The Directive applies to electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) that falls within the categories set out in Annex I, subject to paragraph 2.

per_question.question: How does RoHS Article 3 define electrical and electronic equipment, including the voltage rating?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 3 defines electrical and electronic equipment or EEE as equipment which is dependent on electric currents or electromagnetic fields in order to work properly and equipment for the generation, transfer and measurement of such currents and fields and designed for use with a voltage rating not exceeding 1 000 volts for alternating current and 1 500 volts for direct current.

per_question.question: What does RoHS Article 3 mean by a homogeneous material?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 3 defines a homogeneous material as one material of uniform composition throughout or a material, consisting of a combination of materials, that cannot be disjointed or separated into different materials by mechanical actions such as unscrewing, cutting, crushing, grinding and abrasive processes.
per_question.actual_answer: A homogeneous material is one material of uniform composition throughout or a material consisting of a combination of materials that cannot be disjointed or separated into different materials by mechanical actions such as unscrewing, cutting, crushing, grinding and abrasive processes.

per_question.question: What does RoHS Article 4(1) require Member States to ensure about EEE placed on the market?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 4(1) requires Member States to ensure that EEE placed on the market, including cables and spare parts for its repair, its reuse, updating of its functionalities or upgrading of its capacity, does not contain the substances listed in Annex II.
per_question.actual_answer: Member States shall ensure that EEE placed on the market, including cables and spare parts for its repair, its reuse, updating of its functionalities or upgrading of its capacity, does not contain the substances listed in Annex II.

per_question.question: What does RoHS Article 4(2) say may be tolerated for the substances specified in Annex II?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 4(2) says that no more than the maximum concentration value by weight in homogeneous materials as specified in Annex II shall be tolerated.

per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 6 says a review, based on a thorough assessment, and amendment of the list of restricted substances in Annex II shall be considered by the Commission before 22 July 2014, and periodically thereafter.

per_question.question: What does RoHS Article 7(a) require manufacturers to ensure when placing EEE on the market?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 7(a) requires that, when placing EEE on the market, manufacturers ensure that it has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the requirements set out in Article 4.
per_question.actual_answer: Manufacturers must ensure that the EEE has been designed and manufactured in accordance with the requirements set out in Article 4.

per_question.question: What does RoHS Article 9(a) require importers to place on the Union market?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 9(a) requires that importers place only EEE that complies with this Directive on the Union market.
per_question.actual_answer: Importers must place only electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) that complies with this Directive on the Union market.

per_question.question: What must distributors verify under RoHS Article 10(a) about the CE marking?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 10(a) requires distributors, when making an EEE available on the market, to act with due care in particular by verifying that the EEE bears the CE marking, that it is accompanied by the required documents, and that the manufacturer and the importer have complied with the requirements set out in points (g) and (h) of Article 7 and in point (d) of Article 9.
per_question.actual_answer: Distributors must verify that the EEE bears the CE marking.

per_question.question: When does RoHS Article 11 treat an importer or distributor as a manufacturer?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 11 says an importer or distributor is considered a manufacturer and is subject to the obligations of the manufacturer under Article 7 where he places EEE on the market under his name or trademark or modifies EEE already placed on the market in such a way that compliance with the applicable requirements may be affected.
per_question.actual_answer: When an importer or distributor places electrical and electronic equipment (EEE) on the market under their own name or trademark, or modifies EEE already placed on the market in a way that may affect compliance with the applicable requirements, Article 11 treats them as a manufacturer.

per_question.question: What must the EU declaration of conformity state under RoHS Article 13(1)?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 13(1) says the EU declaration of conformity shall state that it has been demonstrated that the requirements specified in Article 4 have been met.
per_question.actual_answer: The EU declaration of conformity must state that it has been demonstrated that the requirements specified in Article 4 have been met.

per_question.question: How does RoHS Article 15(1) require the CE marking to be affixed?
per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 15(1) says the CE marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly to the finished EEE or to its data plate. Where that is not possible or not warranted on account of the nature of the EEE, it shall be affixed to the packaging and to the accompanying documents.
per_question.actual_answer: The CE marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly to the finished EEE or to its data plate. Where that is not possible or not warranted on account of the nature of the EEE, it shall be affixed to the packaging and to the accompanying documents.

per_question.question: What does RoHS Article 16(1) say Member States shall presume about EEE bearing the CE marking?
per_question.reference_answer: In the absence of evidence to the contrary, RoHS Article 16(1) says Member States shall presume EEE bearing the CE marking to comply with this Directive.
per_question.actual_answer: In the absence of evidence to the contrary, Member States shall presume EEE bearing the CE marking to comply with this Directive.

per_question.reference_answer: RoHS Article 23 says the penalties provided for must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive. The Member States shall notify those provisions to the Commission by 2 January 2013 and shall notify it without delay of any subsequent amendment affecting them.

per_question.question: Who may submit an application for granting, renewing or revoking an exemption under RoHS Annex V?

per_question.question: What purpose does REACH Article 1(1) state for the Regulation?
per_question.reference_answer: REACH Article 1(1) says the purpose of this Regulation is to ensure a high level of protection of human health and the environment, including the promotion of alternative methods for assessment of hazards of substances, as well as the free circulation of substances on the internal market while enhancing competitiveness and innovation.

per_question.question: How does REACH Article 3 define a substance?
per_question.reference_answer: REACH Article 3 defines a substance as a chemical element and its compounds in the natural state or obtained by any manufacturing process, including any additive necessary to preserve its stability and any impurity deriving from the process used, but excluding any solvent which may be separated without affecting the stability of the substance or changing its composition.

per_question.question: What does REACH Article 5 require before manufacture or placing on the market, and which articles qualify that rule?
per_question.reference_answer: Subject to Articles 6, 7, 21 and 23, REACH Article 5 says substances on their own, in mixtures or in articles shall not be manufactured in the Community or placed on the market unless they have been registered in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Title where this is required.
per_question.actual_answer: Article 5 requires that substances on their own, in M3 mixtures or in articles shall not be manufactured in the Community or placed on the market unless they have been registered in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Title where this is required. The rule is subject to Articles 6, 7, 21 and 23.

per_question.question: What quantity triggers registration under REACH Article 6(1), and what does Article 6(2) say about monomers used as isolated intermediates?
per_question.reference_answer: Save where this Regulation provides otherwise, REACH Article 6(1) says any manufacturer or importer of a substance, either on its own or in one or more mixtures, in quantities of one tonne or more per year shall submit a registration to the Agency. Article 6(2) says that for monomers used as on-site isolated intermediates or transported isolated intermediates, Articles 17 and 18 shall not apply.
per_question.actual_answer: Article 6(1) requires registration when a manufacturer or importer produces or imports a substance, on its own or in one or more M3 mixtures, in quantities of one tonne or more per year. Article 6(2) states that for monomers that are used as on‑site isolated intermediates or transported isolated intermediates, Articles 17 and 18 do not apply.

per_question.question: What quantity does REACH Article 7(1)(a) set for a substance present in articles before a producer or importer must consider registration?
per_question.reference_answer: REACH Article 7(1) says any producer or importer of articles shall submit a registration to the Agency for any substance contained in those articles if both stated conditions are met. Condition (a) in the indexed text is that the substance is present in those articles in quantities totalling over one tonne per producer or importer per year.
per_question.actual_answer: over one tonne per producer or importer per year

per_question.question: Whom may a non-Community manufacturer appoint under REACH Article 8(1)?
per_question.reference_answer: REACH Article 8(1) says a natural or legal person established outside the Community who manufactures a substance, formulates a mixture or produces an article that is imported into the Community may by mutual agreement appoint a natural or legal person established in the Community to fulfil, as his only representative, the obligations on importers under this Title.
per_question.actual_answer: A natural or legal person established in the Community.

per_question.question: For how long does REACH Article 9(1) disapply Articles 5, 6, 7, 17, 18 and 21 for product and process orientated research and development?
per_question.reference_answer: REACH Article 9(1) says Articles 5, 6, 7, 17, 18 and 21 shall not apply for a period of five years to a substance manufactured in the Community or imported for the purposes of product and process orientated research and development, in a quantity limited to that purpose.
per_question.actual_answer: REACH Article 9(1) states that Articles 5, 6, 7, 17, 18 and 21 shall not apply for a period of five years to a substance used for product and process orientated research and development.

per_question.question: At what quantity per year does REACH Article 14(1) require a chemical safety assessment and a chemical safety report?
per_question.reference_answer: Without prejudice to Article 4 of Directive 98/24/EC, REACH Article 14(1) says a chemical safety assessment shall be performed and a chemical safety report completed for all substances subject to registration in accordance with this Chapter in quantities of 10 tonnes or more per year per registrant.
per_question.actual_answer: 10 tonnes or more per year per registrant.

per_question.question: What registration duty does REACH Article 17(1) place on a manufacturer of an on-site isolated intermediate?
per_question.reference_answer: REACH Article 17(1) says any manufacturer of an on-site isolated intermediate in quantities of one tonne or more per year shall submit a registration to the Agency for the on-site isolated intermediate.
per_question.actual_answer: Any manufacturer of an on‑site isolated intermediate in quantities of one tonne or more per year shall submit a registration to the Agency for the on‑site isolated intermediate.

per_question.question: Until which date does REACH Article 23(1) disapply Articles 5, 6, 7(1), 17, 18 and 21 for the phase-in substances it lists?

per_question.question: What does REACH Article 25(1) say about testing on vertebrate animals?
per_question.reference_answer: REACH Article 25(1) says that, in order to avoid animal testing, testing on vertebrate animals for the purposes of this Regulation shall be undertaken only as a last resort.
per_question.actual_answer: Article 25(1) states that, in order to avoid animal testing, testing on vertebrate animals for the purposes of this Regulation shall be undertaken only as a last resort, and that measures limiting duplication of other tests are necessary.

per_question.question: In accordance with which annex must a safety data sheet be compiled under REACH Article 31(1)?

per_question.question: Above what concentration does REACH Article 33(1) require information on a substance in an article that meets the Article 57 criteria and is identified under Article 59(1)?

per_question.question: What aim does REACH Article 55 state for the authorisation title?
